title: Uniform machine code
statement: A uniform machine code consists of an effective machine code, a Boolean finite-tape machine, and a natural number $d$. For every pair of Boolean strings $\alpha,x$ and every $t\in\mathbb N$, if the machine decoded from $\alpha$ outputs $[\mathrm{true}]$ on $x$ in exactly $t$ steps, the simulator outputs $[\mathrm{true}]$ on the encoding of the three inputs $\operatorname{bits}(t),\alpha,x$ in at most the specified time $d\,(|\alpha|+|x|+t+1)^d$; if it does not output $[\mathrm{true}]$ on $x$ in exactly $t$ steps, the simulator outputs $[\mathrm{false}]$ on that encoding within the same time bound.
hypotheses_covered: A natural-number degree and coefficient d
For all Boolean strings α and x and all natural numbers t, correct bounded-acceptance output within the stated bound
